Let \(n=3q\) and \(e_N(t)=\exp(2\pi i t/N)\). Write
\[
A_q(r)=\sum_{x\bmod 3^n} e_{3^n}(x^3-rx).
\]

We use three elementary facts.

First, replacing \(x\) by \(x+3^{n-1}t\), \(t\bmod 3\), changes the phase by \(-rt/3\). Hence
\[
A_q(r)=0\qquad (3\nmid r).
\]

Second, if \(r=9R\), then all unit classes \(x\not\equiv0\pmod3\) cancel by the same one-step summation in the next digit, while the class \(x=3y\) gives
\[
A_q(9R)
=\sum_{y\bmod 3^{n-1}} e_{3^n}(27y^3-27Ry)
=9A_{q-1}(R).
\]
Since \(R\) is taken modulo \(3^{3q-3}\), each residue for \(A_{q-1}\) has exactly \(3\) lifts to a residue \(r\bmod 3^{3q}\). Thus the contribution from \(9\mid r\) is
\[
3P_{q-1},\qquad 3N_{q-1}.
\]

Third, consider \(r=3s\) with \(3\nmid s\). If \(s\equiv2\pmod3\), there is no solution to \(x^2\equiv s\pmod3\), so stationary-phase summation gives \(A_q(3s)=0\). If \(s\equiv1\pmod3\), choose the unique \(a\bmod 3^{n-1}\) with
\[
a^2\equiv s\pmod{3^{n-1}},\qquad a\equiv1\pmod3.
\]
The two critical classes are \(a\) and \(-a\), and the local quadratic factors are equal positive real multiples of conjugate phases, giving
\[
\operatorname{sgn} A_q(3s)
=
\operatorname{sgn}\cos\!\left(\frac{4\pi a^3}{3^n}\right).
\]

Now the cube map sends
\[
a\bmod 3^{n-1},\quad a\equiv1\pmod3
\]
bijectively onto
\[
y\bmod 3^n,\quad y\equiv1\pmod9.
\]
Therefore we only need to count residues \(y\equiv1\pmod9\) for which
\[
\cos\!\left(\frac{4\pi y}{3^n}\right)>0.
\]
This holds for
\[
0<y<\frac{3^n}{8},\qquad
\frac{3\cdot 3^n}{8}<y<\frac{5\cdot 3^n}{8},\qquad
\frac{7\cdot 3^n}{8}<y<3^n.
\]
There are \(3^{n-2}=3^{3q-2}\) residues \(y\equiv1\pmod9\). A direct floor count, using
\[
3^n\equiv
\begin{cases}
9\pmod{72},&q\text{ even},\\
27\pmod{72},&q\text{ odd},
\end{cases}
\]
gives
\[
U_q^+=\frac{3^{3q-2}+(-1)^q}{2},\qquad
U_q^-=\frac{3^{3q-2}-(-1)^q}{2}
\]
for the positive and negative values among \(r=3s\), \(3\nmid s\).

For \(q=1\), direct evaluation gives
\[
(P_1,N_1)=(4,2).
\]
Thus for \(q\ge2\),
\[
P_q=3P_{q-1}+U_q^+,\qquad
N_q=3N_{q-1}+U_q^-.
\]
Adding and subtracting,
\[
P_q+N_q=3(P_{q-1}+N_{q-1})+3^{3q-2},
\]
\[
P_q-N_q=3(P_{q-1}-N_{q-1})+(-1)^q.
\]
Solving these recurrences from \((P_1,N_1)=(4,2)\),
\[
P_q+N_q=\frac{3^{3q}+21\cdot 3^{q-1}}{8},
\]
\[
P_q-N_q=\frac{3^{q+1}+(-1)^q}{4}.
\]
Hence
\[
P_q=\frac{3^{3q}+39\cdot 3^{q-1}+2(-1)^q}{16},
\]
\[
N_q=\frac{3^{3q}+3^q-2(-1)^q}{16}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(P_q,N_q\right)=\left(\frac{3^{3q}+39\cdot 3^{q-1}+2(-1)^q}{16},\frac{3^{3q}+3^q-2(-1)^q}{16}\right)}
\]
